title: CDU-4 startup procedure
question: What is the approved CDU-4 startup sequence? Explain pre-start readiness, warm-up, monitoring points, hold conditions and handover, and generate a practical startup checklist document.

answer.summary: The startup SOP divides the process into pre-start readiness, controlled warm-up, monitoring, hold conditions and handover.
details: Before start: confirm maintenance handback, verify utilities, check line-up, review permits and confirm control-room/field communications.
Warm-up: establish circulation, begin controlled heating, stabilize column pressure, introduce crude at reduced rate and increase feed in planned steps.
Monitor furnace outlet temperature, column pressure, feed flow, desalter differential pressure and reflux stability.
Hold conditions include loss of instrument air, unstable pressure, hydrocarbon leak, critical instrument failure and utility instability.
During handover, record startup time and deviations, remove/control temporary overrides and transfer stable operation to normal monitoring.

title: Permit-to-work and energy isolation
question: For planned maintenance on a pump, explain how permit-to-work and energy isolation should work together. Cover permit selection, hazards, P-102 isolation boundaries, zero-energy verification, lockout and restoration, and produce a one-page procedural PDF with a flow diagram.

answer.summary: Permit-to-work identifies the work authorization and field controls; energy isolation identifies and controls the hazardous energy sources. They must be coordinated before work begins and verified before personnel are exposed.
details: Permit selection depends on the work type: hot work, confined space, electrical work, line breaking or work at height.
Hazard identification includes hydrocarbon release, pressure, temperature, electrical energy, stored mechanical energy and toxic exposure.
For P-102, the energy-isolation boundary includes M-102 electrical supply, process suction isolation, process discharge isolation, drain/vent as required and stored rotational energy.
Lockout uses individual locks where required, with a group lockbox for multi-person work and a formal exception process for lock removal.
Zero-energy verification includes absence-of-voltage testing, pressure confirmation, drain verification and an approved try-start where safe.
Restoration requires work completion, guards installed, tools removed, locks cleared, line-up restored and operations acceptance.

execution_steps: Identify the maintenance task and required permit type.
Retrieve Permit-to-Work SOP and Energy Isolation SOP.
Resolve P-102-specific isolation boundary from process/tag records.
Build a combined permit/isolation sequence.
Generate PDF and flow diagram.
Do not invent site-specific permit numbers or approvals.
